官方样题 · British Council · Academic Practice Test 2 · Miles Davis · Q14–19 · PDF 第 1, 2 页

Choose the correct heading for each paragraph from the list of headings. Write the correct Roman numeral, i–ix. 本组保留原题号；同一标题不可重复使用。

AAt the age of thirteen, Miles Davis was given his first trumpet, lessons were arranged with a local trumpet player, and a musical odyssey began. These early lessons, paid for and supported by his father, had a profound effect on shaping Davis’ signature sound. Whereas most trumpeters of the era favoured the use of vibrato (a wobbly quiver in pitch inflected in the instrument’s tone), Davis was taught to play with a long, straight tone, a preference his instructor reportedly drilled into the young trumpeter with a rap on the knuckles every time Davis began using vibrato. This clear, distinctive style never left Davis. He continued playing with it for the rest of his career, once remarking, ‘If I can’t get that sound, I can’t play anything.’

BHaving graduated from high school in 1944, Davis moved to New York City, where he continued his musical education both in the clubs and in the classroom. His enrolment in the prestigious Julliard School of Music was short-lived, however – he soon dropped out, criticising what he perceived as an over-emphasis on the classical European repertoire and a neglect of jazz. Davis did later acknowledge, however, that this time at the school was invaluable in terms of developing his trumpet-playing technique and giving him a solid grounding in music theory. Much of his early training took place in the form of jam sessions and performances in the clubs of 52nd Street, where he played alongside both up- and-coming and established members of the jazz pantheon such as Coleman Hawkins, Eddie ‘Lockjaw’ Davis, and Thelonious Monk.

CIn the late 1940s, Davis collaborated with nine other instrumentalists, including a French horn and a tuba player, to produce The Birth of Cool, an album now renowned for the inchoate sounds of what would later become known as ‘cool’ jazz. In contrast to popular jazz styles of the day, which featured rapid, rollicking beats, shrieking vocals, and short, sharp horn blasts, Davis’ album was the forerunner of a different kind of sound – thin, light horn-playing, hushed drums and a more restrained, formal arrangement. Although it received little acclaim at the time (the liner notes to one of Davis’ later recordings call it a ‘spectacular failure’), in hindsight The Birth of Cool has become recognised as a pivotal moment in jazz history, cementing – alongside his 1958 recording, Kind of Blue – Davis’ legacy as one of the most innovative musicians of his era.

He continued playing with it for the rest of his career, once remarking, ‘If I can’t get that sound, I can’t play anything.’A段从十三岁获得小号写起。父亲资助的课程塑造了他的标志性音色：当时许多演奏者偏爱颤音，他的老师却训练他保持悠长、平直的音。后来的自述表明，这种音色成为他认同自身演奏的基础。原文描述老师敲打指关节的做法，是人物经历，不是认可这种教学方式。BHaving graduated from high school in 1944, Davis moved to New York City, where he continued his musical education both in the clubs and in the classroom. His enrolment in the prestigious Julliard School of Music was short-lived, however – he soon dropped out, criticising what he perceived as an over-emphasis on the classical European repertoire and a neglect of jazz. Davis did later acknowledge, however, that this time at the school was invaluable in terms of developing his trumpet-playing technique and giving him a solid grounding in music theory. Much of his early training took place in the form of jam sessions and performances in the clubs of 52nd Street, where he played alongside both up- and-coming and established members of the jazz pantheon such as Coleman Hawkins, Eddie ‘Lockjaw’ Davis, and Thelonious Monk.B段把音乐教育分为学校课堂和俱乐部两种环境。戴维斯不满学校偏重欧洲古典曲目、忽视爵士，因而退学；但他后来仍肯定学校对小号技巧和乐理基础的帮助。与新秀和成名乐手同台的经历，则提供了课堂之外的实践。两种学习来源并非互相排斥。CIn the late 1940s, Davis collaborated with nine other instrumentalists, including a French horn and a tuba player, to produce The Birth of Cool, an album now renowned for the inchoate sounds of what would later become known as ‘cool’ jazz. In contrast to popular jazz styles of the day, which featured rapid, rollicking beats, shrieking vocals, and short, sharp horn blasts, Davis’ album was the forerunner of a different kind of sound – thin, light horn-playing, hushed drums and a more restrained, formal arrangement. Although it received little acclaim at the time (the liner notes to one of Davis’ later recordings call it a ‘spectacular failure’), in hindsight The Birth of Cool has become recognised as a pivotal moment in jazz history, cementing – alongside his 1958 recording, Kind of Blue – Davis’ legacy as one of the most innovative musicians of his era.C段将前面的个人风格推进到合作录音。他与其他乐器演奏者创造了较轻、克制、编排更正式的声音，与当时流行的急促节拍和强烈音响形成对照。作品当时缺少赞誉，后来却被视为爵士史的重要转折。in hindsight明确区分当时反响与后来的评价。词语与搭配had a profound effect on对……产生深远影响have an effect on后接受到影响的人、事或过程；profound强调影响深而持久，此处具体指早期课程塑造音色。a solid grounding in music theory扎实的乐理基础grounding表示作为后续学习或实践基础的知识训练，常与in搭配；不是地面或被禁足的意思。In contrast to与……形成对照后接名词性成分，此处引出当时流行爵士与新录音在声音上的差异，不表示其中一方天然更好。in hindsight事后回看；从后来的认识看用于区分经历发生时与后来回顾时的理解；不能把后来获得的评价写成当时已经普遍接受。句子精读Whereas most trumpeters of the era favoured the use of vibrato (a wobbly quiver in pitch inflected in the instrument’s tone), Davis was taught to play with a long, straight tone, a preference his instructor reportedly drilled into the young trumpeter with a rap on the knuckles every time Davis began using vibrato.当时大多数小号演奏者喜欢运用颤音，即乐器音色中音高的颤动；戴维斯却被教导使用悠长、平直的音。据说，每当他开始使用颤音时，老师就敲一下他的指关节，以此把这种偏好灌输给他。Whereas引出对照；括号解释vibrato。a preference补充说明前面的演奏取向，his instructor reportedly drilled into...说明训练方式；reportedly表明这一细节来自转述。every time引出每次发生的情形。Davis did later acknowledge, however, that this time at the school was invaluable in terms of developing his trumpet-playing technique and giving him a solid grounding in music theory.不过，戴维斯后来确实承认，在这所学校的经历对发展他的小号演奏技巧、打下扎实的乐理基础非常宝贵。did强调他确实作过这一肯定；that引出承认的内容。in terms of后面developing和giving并列，指出两方面价值。this time指在学校学习的这段经历，不能因他退学就把学校贡献一并否定。这篇材料里可用于写作的表达a solid grounding in music theory扎实的乐理基础可说明专业理论如何支持实践；不把理论学习与工作实习写成只能二选一。用于写作：自编例句，适用于本科课程是否应包括实习：音乐专业作为具体例子，说明已有理论知识怎样在工作环境中应用；不代表所有专业都需要录音棚实习。读完讲解，可以把原文连起来再读一次；想保留的词句可使用已有收藏功能。
